b2-01.q: Which sentence correctly expresses an unlikely, hypothetical situation?
options: Si tuviera más tiempo, buscaría en los registros civiles.
Si tendría más tiempo, buscaría en los registros civiles.
Si tengo más tiempo, buscaría en los registros civiles.
Si tuviera más tiempo, buscara en los registros civiles.
b2-01.why: Hypothetical: si + imperfect subjunctive (tuviera) + conditional (buscaría). *Si tendría copies English 'if I would'; si tengo needs a future result (buscaré); buscara in the result clause is not standard.

b2-01.q: In «Aunque ella ya no (vivir) allí, quiero ir a verla», the speaker does not know whether she still lives there. Which form fits?
b2-01.why: Aunque + present subjunctive presents the point as hypothetical: 'even if she no longer lives there'. Vive would assert as a fact that she has moved.

b2-01.q: What does «Por difícil que parezca, lo encontraremos» mean?
options: Because it seems difficult, we will find it.
It seems difficult, so we will not find it.
It seems difficult for us to find it.
However difficult it may seem, we will find it.
b2-01.why: Por + adjective + que + subjunctive is concessive: 'however difficult'. Por here does not mean 'because'.

b2-01.q: What does «Alguien debió de esconder las cartas allí» mean?
options: Someone must have hidden the letters there.
Someone should have hidden the letters there.
Someone had to hide the letters there.
Someone was supposed to hide the letters there.
b2-01.why: Deber de + infinitive expresses a guess: debió de esconder = 'must have hidden'. Obligation ('should have') is deber without de: debió esconder / debería haber escondido.

b2-01.q: Correct the error: «Si tendría más tiempo, saldría ahora mismo a preguntar por el puerto.» Tendría should be:
b2-01.why: A hypothetical if-clause takes the imperfect subjunctive: si tuviera..., saldría. The conditional never follows si meaning 'if'.

b2-01.q: Elvira knows Tomás is dead, yet says «Aunque él ya no esté para oírlo...». Why the subjunctive?
options: She concedes a known fact but treats it as irrelevant to her point.
She doubts that Tomás is really dead.
b2-01.why: Aunque + subjunctive can concede a shared, known fact ('even though') while presenting it as not mattering. Doubt is not implied, and aunque takes the indicative when the speaker asserts new information.

b2-01.q: Complete: «Ignacio pensaba que, por difícil que (ser), encontraría a la destinataria.»
b2-01.why: Por + adjective + que needs the subjunctive, and in a past context (pensaba... encontraría) the imperfect subjunctive: fuera.

b2-01.q: Which sentence means 'You should tell your boss about the letter' (obligation)?
options: Debes contarle a tu jefe lo de la carta.
Debes de contarle a tu jefe lo de la carta.
Debe de habérselo contado a su jefe.
Tienes de contarle a tu jefe lo de la carta.
b2-01.why: Obligation is deber + infinitive with no de. Deber de expresses probability (the third option means 'he must have told his boss'), and using it for obligation is considered incorrect. Tener que, not *tener de.

b2-02.q: Complete: «Don Aurelio miraba la cocina como si (ser) un extraño.»
b2-02.why: Como si takes only the imperfect (or pluperfect) subjunctive: fuera. Indicative and conditional are never used after como si.

options: Si cambiaríamos la receta, los clientes se quejarían.
Si cambiamos la receta, los clientes se quejarán.
Si cambiáramos la receta, los clientes se quejarían.
Los clientes se quejarían si cambiáramos la receta.
b2-02.why: The conditional cannot go in the if-clause: si cambiáramos. The other three are correct: a real possibility (cambiamos... quejarán) and a hypothetical in either order.

b2-02.q: Which sentence expresses an unlikely or impossible wish ('I wish she could taste it')?
b2-02.why: Ojalá + imperfect subjunctive expresses an unlikely or impossible wish. Ojalá never takes the conditional, and the indicative after ojalá is non-standard.

b2-02.q: Complete: «No era que don Aurelio ___ terco por naturaleza; ___ asustado.»
b2-02.why: Being stubborn 'by nature' is a characteristic: ser (here subjunctive fuera after no era que). Being frightened is a state: estaba asustado.

options: Camila habla de la fonda como si fuera suya.
Camila habla de la fonda como si sea suya.
Camila habla de la fonda como si es suya.
Camila habla de la fonda como si sería suya.
b2-02.why: Even with a present main verb (habla), como si takes the imperfect subjunctive. The present subjunctive is never used after como si.

b2-02.q: Camila says: «Si cambiáramos la receta, los clientes se quejarían.» What does her choice of tense suggest?
options: She sees changing the recipe as an imagined, unlikely step.
She has decided to change the recipe tomorrow.
She changed the recipe and the customers complained.
She is asking whether she should change the recipe.
b2-02.why: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional presents the condition as hypothetical. A real plan would be si cambiamos..., se quejarán.

b2-02.q: Complete: «Por mucho que mañana (insistir) los clientes, Camila no va a hacer el plato idéntico.»
b2-02.why: Por mucho que + subjunctive; the context is future (mañana, va a hacer), so present subjunctive: insistan.

b2-02.q: What does «Don Aurelio está malo» mean?
options: Don Aurelio is a bad person.
Don Aurelio is bad at cooking.
b2-02.why: Malo changes meaning: estar malo = 'to be ill'; ser malo = 'to be bad/wicked'. Compare listo (clever/ready) and rico (rich/tasty).

b2-03.q: Complete: «La alcaldesa pidió que se (organizar) una visita al parque eólico.»
b2-03.why: Verbs of request take the subjunctive, and after the past verb pidió it is the imperfect subjunctive: organizara.

b2-03.q: Which translation fits «Si los molinos se levantaran sobre la loma, las ovejas perderían el pasto»?
options: If the windmills went up on the ridge, the sheep would lose their pasture.
If the windmills go up on the ridge, the sheep will lose their pasture.
If the windmills had gone up on the ridge, the sheep would have lost their pasture.
When the windmills went up on the ridge, the sheep lost their pasture.
b2-03.why: Imperfect subjunctive + conditional is a hypothetical about the present or future ('went up... would lose'). The pluperfect subjunctive would be needed for 'had gone up'.

b2-03.q: Which sentence correctly uses passive se ('Passionate arguments were heard')?
b2-03.why: With passive se the verb agrees with the thing affected: alegatos is plural, so se oyeron. Se always comes before a conjugated verb.

b2-03.q: Complete: «Pilar habla del proyecto como si ya (estar) aprobado.»
b2-03.why: Como si takes the imperfect subjunctive even after a present main verb. *Como si esté and *como si está are typical learner errors.

options: La alcaldesa quería que los vecinos vieran los molinos.
La alcaldesa quería que los vecinos verían los molinos.
La alcaldesa quería los vecinos ver los molinos.
La alcaldesa quería que los vecinos ven los molinos.
b2-03.why: Querer que + subjunctive when the subject changes; after a past verb, imperfect subjunctive: vieran. Spanish cannot copy English 'wanted them to see'.

b2-03.q: Which phrase is the standard way to give advice like English 'If I were you...'?
b2-03.why: Si yo fuera usted (or tú) + conditional is the fixed formula for advice: si yo fuera usted, exigiría garantías.

b2-03.q: Complete: «En el pleno se (presentar) dos propuestas.»
b2-03.why: Passive se agrees with the noun: dos propuestas is plural, so se presentaron. A singular verb (se presentó) would need a singular noun.

b2-03.q: «Anselmo siguió comiendo como si nada hubiera pasado.» What does hubiera pasado add compared with pasara?
options: It refers to an imagined event earlier than the eating: 'as if nothing had happened'.
It shows that something really happened later.
It expresses Anselmo's uncertainty about the future.
Nothing: hubiera pasado and pasara are always interchangeable.
b2-03.why: After como si, the imperfect subjunctive is simultaneous (as if nothing were happening) and the pluperfect subjunctive is anterior (as if nothing had happened).

b2-04.q: Which sentence correctly expresses an unreal past condition?
options: Si lo hubiera escrito yo, habría sido más elegante.
Si lo habría escrito yo, hubiera sido más elegante.
Si lo había escrito yo, habría sido más elegante.
Si lo hubiera escrito yo, habrá sido más elegante.
b2-04.why: Unreal past: si + hubiera + participle, habría (or hubiera) + participle. The conditional and the pluperfect indicative do not go in the if-clause, and habrá is a future perfect.

b2-04.topic: Ojalá and como si with pluperfect
b2-04.q: What does «Ojalá hubiera tenido esa libertad» express?
options: Regret: I wish I had had that freedom.
A hope that I will have that freedom.
A fact: I had that freedom.
A wish that I could have that freedom now.
b2-04.why: Ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive expresses regret about the past. 'I wish I had it now' would be ojalá tuviera.

b2-04.q: Complete: «Por mucho que me lo (pedir) mañana, no cambiaré la frase.»
b2-04.why: With a future outcome, por mucho que must take the subjunctive, here present subjunctive: pida. Pidiera would not match the future cambiaré.

b2-04.q: «Quizá les mentí.» Rewrite it with «Es posible que...»:
b2-04.why: Es posible que always takes the subjunctive; for a past event use the imperfect subjunctive (mintiera) or the present perfect subjunctive (haya mentido).

b2-04.q: «Si hubieras leído el correo del autor, no me pedirías lo contrario.» When is the asking happening?
options: Now: a past condition with a present result.
In the past: both halves refer to the past.
It is an error; it must be habrías pedido.
b2-04.why: This is a mixed conditional: pluperfect subjunctive for the past condition, simple conditional for the present consequence ('you wouldn't be asking me').

b2-04.topic: Ojalá and como si with pluperfect
b2-04.q: Complete the regret: «Ojalá ___ en aquella reunión; ahora ya es tarde.»
b2-04.why: Regret about a past that cannot change: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Me haya callado would mean 'I hope I kept quiet' (outcome unknown).

b2-04.q: In «un hombre que, aunque sea discreto, ha decidido contar su verdad», what does aunque sea discreto mean?
options: Discreet though he may be (his discretion is accepted but does not stop him).
If he becomes discreet in the future.
Although he is definitely not discreet.
b2-04.why: Aunque + subjunctive here concedes something the speaker accepts and presents it as irrelevant to the main point.

options: Es posible que les haya mentido.
A lo mejor les haya mentido.
b2-04.why: A lo mejor always takes the indicative (a lo mejor les mintió). Puede que and es posible que take the subjunctive.

b2-05.q: Complete: «Si me lo hubieras dicho, me (ahorrar) tres noches sin dormir.»
b2-05.why: The result of an unreal past condition takes the conditional perfect: habría ahorrado (hubiera ahorrado is also correct). Ahorraría would refer to the present.

b2-05.q: What does «Aunque hubieras permanecido callado, otro habría hablado» mean?
options: Although you stayed silent, someone else spoke.
Even if you had stayed silent, someone else would have spoken.
Even if you stay silent, someone else will speak.
Because you stayed silent, someone else spoke.
b2-05.why: Aunque + pluperfect subjunctive imagines a past that did not happen and says it would not have changed the outcome.

b2-05.q: Which sentence uses passive se correctly?
options: Se concederían una prima a los equipos.
Se concedería unas primas a los equipos.
Se concedería una prima a los equipos.
Se concedieron una prima a los equipos.
b2-05.why: Passive se agrees with the noun: singular una prima takes singular concedería; plural primas would need concederían.

b2-05.q: In the story (told in the past, long after the meeting), the boss said: «No habrá despidos.» Which report is the standard one?
options: Comunicó que no había habido despidos.
b2-05.why: In past narration the future becomes the conditional: habrá becomes habría. Habrá is kept only when the event is still in the future at the moment of reporting.

b2-05.q: Correct the error: «Si me lo habrías dicho antes, no habría hablado.» Habrías dicho should be:
b2-05.why: The if-clause of an unreal past condition takes the pluperfect subjunctive: si me lo hubieras dicho. English 'if you would have told me' causes this error.

b2-05.q: Which sentence means 'I wish I had kept quiet on Monday'?
options: Ojalá me hubiera callado el lunes.
Ojalá me habría callado el lunes.
b2-05.why: Past regret: ojalá + pluperfect subjunctive. Ojalá me calle el lunes is a hope about next Monday; ojalá never takes the conditional or indicative.

b2-05.q: Complete: «Contra lo que decía el rumor, solo se (despedir) a dos contables.»
b2-05.why: With people introduced by personal a, se is impersonal and the verb stays singular: se despidió a dos contables. *Se despidieron a dos contables is a frequent but non-standard mix.

b2-05.q: In «Comunicó que no habría despidos», what does habría express?
options: A future seen from the past: there would be no layoffs afterwards.
A hypothetical: there would be no layoffs if something happened.
A guess: there were probably no layoffs.
b2-05.why: In reported speech the conditional is the future-in-the-past: it reports «no habrá despidos». It is not a hypothetical 'would'.

b2-06.q: Which sentence means 'If I had known, I would have closed the drawer'?
options: Si lo hubiera sabido, habría cerrado el cajón.
Si lo había sabido, habría cerrado el cajón.
Si lo hubiera sabido, cerraría el cajón.
Si lo habría sabido, hubiera cerrado el cajón.
b2-06.why: Unreal past: si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect. Cerraría would mean 'I would close it (now)'; habría and había cannot follow si in an unreal condition.

b2-06.q: Direct speech: «Encontré un resguardo.» How is it reported after «Dijo que...»?
options: Dijo que había encontrado un resguardo.
b2-06.why: After a past reporting verb, a preterite shifts back to the pluperfect: había encontrado. (In speech, dijo que encontró is also common.) Encontraba changes the meaning to an ongoing action.

b2-06.topic: Subjunctive in time and relative clauses
b2-06.q: Complete: «El dueño prometió que volvería cuando el reloj (estar) listo.»
b2-06.why: Cuando takes the subjunctive for an action still pending; seen from the past (prometió, volvería) that is the imperfect subjunctive: estuviera.

b2-06.q: Complete: «Ese reloj no ___ en venta y no ___ asunto tuyo.»
b2-06.why: Estar en venta is a fixed expression for a situation ('for sale'); ser identifies or classifies: es asunto tuyo.

b2-06.q: What does «De haberlo sabido, habría cerrado el cajón» mean?
options: Had I known, I would have closed the drawer.
Since I knew, I closed the drawer.
When I find out, I will close the drawer.
I should have known and closed the drawer.
b2-06.why: De + perfect infinitive is a literary alternative to si + pluperfect subjunctive: de haberlo sabido = si lo hubiera sabido.

b2-06.q: Remedios had said: «No lo arregle hasta que pueda soportar oírlo.» Complete the report: «Me rogó que no lo ___ hasta que pudiera soportar oírlo.»
b2-06.why: A reported request or order becomes que + subjunctive; after the past rogó it is the imperfect subjunctive: arreglara.

b2-06.topic: Subjunctive in time and relative clauses
b2-06.q: In «Mientras ese reloj estuviera parado, ella tenía un motivo para volver», mientras means:
b2-06.why: Mientras + subjunctive is conditional ('as long as'); mientras + indicative means 'while' (mientras él trabajaba...).

b2-06.q: Which sentence describes the resulting state rather than the action?
options: El cajón estaba cerrado con llave.
El cajón fue cerrado con llave por el maestro.
El cajón se cerró con un chirrido.
El maestro cerró el cajón con llave.
b2-06.why: Estar + participle = resulting state. Ser + participle and se + verb describe the action of closing.

b2-07.q: Direct speech: «El artículo saldrá el domingo.» The story is told in the past and that Sunday is long gone. Which report fits?
options: Anunció que el artículo saldría el domingo.
Anunció que el artículo saldrá el domingo.
Anunció que el artículo salió el domingo.
Anunció que el artículo salga el domingo.
b2-07.why: After a past reporting verb the future becomes the conditional: saldría. Saldrá is possible only if the Sunday is still in the future when you speak.

b2-07.q: Complete: «No fue ella ___ desveló el nombre del remitente, sino un antiguo contable.»
b2-07.why: In cleft sentences use quien (or la que) for a person. El cual / la cual and bare cual are not used to introduce the clause in a cleft.

options: Si hubiera existido otro modo, lo habría usado.
Si hubiese existido otro modo, lo habría usado.
Si hubiera existido otro modo, lo hubiera usado.
Si habría existido otro modo, lo hubiera usado.
b2-07.why: The conditional (habría) cannot go in the if-clause. Hubiera and hubiese are interchangeable after si, and hubiera can replace habría in the result.

b2-07.q: Doña Matilde means 'even if it makes me look bad' (a possibility). Complete: «Te pido que escribas todo, aunque me (dejar) mal.»
b2-07.why: Aunque + present subjunctive presents the consequence as a possibility that does not matter: deje. Deja would assert it as a fact.

b2-07.q: Gustavo said: «Habría preferido el titular sencillo.» Complete the report: «Gustavo admitió que ___ el titular sencillo.»
b2-07.why: The conditional perfect does not change in reported speech: admitió que habría preferido.

b2-07.q: Which sentence highlights the remark as the thing that made her hesitate?
options: Fue ese comentario el que la hizo dudar.
Fue ese comentario quien la hizo dudar.
Era ese comentario cual la hizo dudar.
b2-07.why: For a thing, use el/la que agreeing with the focus (comentario: el que). Quien is only for people; the plain sentence has no special emphasis.

b2-07.q: Which statement about «Si se hubiese tratado de un funcionario cualquiera...» is true?
options: After si, hubiese and hubiera are interchangeable.
Hubiese is used only in Spain.
Hubiese is more informal than hubiera.
b2-07.why: The -se and -ra forms of the imperfect/pluperfect subjunctive are interchangeable after si; -se is slightly more formal and less frequent, especially in Latin America.

b2-07.q: Complete: «Lo que no soportaría es que ___ solo la parte que me favorece.»
b2-07.why: Soportar que (emotion/tolerance) takes the subjunctive; after the conditional soportaría, the imperfect subjunctive: contaras.

b2-08.q: Matías said: «Encontramos el dinero en un cajón.» Complete the report: «Matías explicó que ___ el dinero en un cajón.»
b2-08.why: A preterite in direct speech becomes the pluperfect after a past reporting verb: habían encontrado (in speech, encontraron is also heard).

b2-08.q: Which is correct for 'You were the one who left'?
b2-08.why: Ser agrees with the pronoun (fuiste tú); after quien the verb is normally third person (se marchó). A bare que after a person is avoided in careful Spanish.

b2-08.q: In «No ir habría equivalido a confesar que todavía me dolía», what does no ir express?
b2-08.why: The conditional perfect can stand alone when the condition is expressed by another element, here the infinitive: no ir = si no hubiera ido.

b2-08.topic: Quien and lo que in relative clauses
b2-08.q: Complete: «___ recuerdas es lo que te ha servido para vivir tranquilo.»
b2-08.why: English 'what' meaning 'the thing that' is lo que. Qué is for questions, and el cual / lo cual need an antecedent.

b2-08.q: «Yo había pasado dos décadas convencido de que me habían tomado por un ladrón.» Which happened first?
options: They (he believed) took him for a thief; then he spent two decades convinced of it.
He spent two decades convinced; then they took him for a thief.
Both happened at exactly the same time.
They will take him for a thief after the reunion.
b2-08.why: The pluperfect habían tomado marks an event before another past point (the two decades of conviction).

b2-08.q: Which is correct for 'It was I who paid for the round'?
options: Fui yo quien pagó la ronda.
Fue yo quien pagó la ronda.
Fui yo quien pagaste la ronda.
Era yo que pagó la ronda.
b2-08.why: Ser agrees with yo (fui), and after quien the verb is normally third person (pagó).

b2-08.q: Complete: «Si de verdad ___ que habías robado, no habríamos insistido tanto.»
b2-08.why: Unreal past condition: si + pluperfect subjunctive (hubiéramos creído) + conditional perfect (habríamos insistido).

b2-08.topic: Quien and lo que in relative clauses
b2-08.q: Complete: «Quien (llegar) más tarde pagará la primera ronda.»
b2-08.why: Quien without an antecedent refers to an unidentified person, and with a future main verb it takes the subjunctive: quien llegue.

b2-09.q: What does «Serían las tres de la madrugada» mean?
options: It would be three in the morning tomorrow.
It must have been about three in the morning.
It was exactly three in the morning.
It will be three in the morning.
b2-09.why: The conditional can express a guess about the past: serían las tres = 'it must have been (about) three'.

b2-09.q: Complete: «En el museo no había nadie que (saber) arreglar la caja de música.»
b2-09.why: A non-existent antecedent (no había nadie) requires the subjunctive, and in a past context the imperfect subjunctive: supiera.

b2-09.topic: Si-clauses with pluperfect and imperfect subjunctive
b2-09.q: Which sentence imagines an unlikely situation in the present or future?
options: Si alguien lo reparara, ella le daría las gracias.
Si alguien lo hubiera reparado, ella le habría dado las gracias.
Si alguien lo reparó, ella le dio las gracias.
Si alguien lo reparaba, ella le daba las gracias.
b2-09.why: Si + imperfect subjunctive + conditional is a present/future hypothetical. Pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect is an unreal past; the indicative options describe real past events or habits.

b2-09.q: Direct speech: «El mecanismo está roto.» How is it reported after «Ella respondió que...»?
options: Ella respondió que el mecanismo está roto.
Ella respondió que el mecanismo estaba roto.
Ella respondió que el mecanismo estuvo roto.
Ella respondió que el mecanismo estaría roto.
b2-09.why: After a past reporting verb, the present becomes the imperfect: está becomes estaba.

b2-09.q: Express a guess about the present: 'It must be the radio.' → «___ la radio.»
b2-09.why: A guess about the present uses the future (será); the conditional (sería) is for a guess about the past.

b2-09.q: Which sentence refers to a specific person the speaker already knows?
options: Busco a la vigilante que habla quechua.
Busco a alguien que hable quechua.
No conozco a nadie que hable quechua.
b2-09.why: A known, specific antecedent takes the indicative (habla). Unknown, questioned or non-existent antecedents take the subjunctive.

b2-09.topic: Si-clauses with pluperfect and imperfect subjunctive
b2-09.q: The curator said: «Si alguien lograra repararlo, le erigiría una estatua.» Complete the report: «Respondió que, si alguien ___ repararlo, le erigiría una estatua.»
b2-09.why: A hypothetical with the imperfect subjunctive does not change in reported speech: si alguien lograra... le erigiría.

b2-09.q: Efraín said: «Un visitante me lo preguntó.» Which is the backshifted report?
options: Efraín inventó que un visitante se lo había preguntado.
Efraín inventó que un visitante se lo preguntaría.
Efraín inventó que un visitante se lo pregunte.
Efraín inventó que un visitante se lo ha preguntado.
b2-09.why: A preterite becomes the pluperfect after a past reporting verb; me also becomes se (le → se before lo) because the speaker changes.

b2-10.q: Which sentence is correct for 'Had the envelope come on Monday, we would have had time'?
options: Si el sobre hubiese llegado el lunes, habríamos tenido tiempo.
Si el sobre había llegado el lunes, habríamos tenido tiempo.
Si el sobre habría llegado el lunes, hubiésemos tenido tiempo.
Si el sobre hubiese llegado el lunes, habremos tenido tiempo.
b2-10.why: Unreal past: si + hubiese/hubiera + participle, habríamos + participle. Spanish has no inverted 'had the envelope come'.

b2-10.q: Complete: «Fue en el verano de 1994 ___ se secó el pozo.»
b2-10.why: When the focus is a time expression, the cleft uses cuando (donde for places, como for manner). Fue en 1994 que is common in Latin American speech but cuando is preferred.

b2-10.q: Evaristo had already voted by post. What does «Nadie sabía a quién habría votado Evaristo» mean?
options: Nobody knew who Evaristo might have voted for.
Nobody knew who Evaristo would vote for if he could.
Nobody knew who Evaristo had to vote for.
Nobody knew who Evaristo will vote for.
b2-10.why: Here the conditional perfect expresses conjecture about a past event (the vote already cast), not a hypothetical 'would have'.

b2-10.q: What does «Ocurra lo que ocurra, no impugnaré nada» mean?
options: Whatever happens, I will not contest anything.
If something happens, I will contest it.
What happened is that I contested nothing.
Something occurs, and I do not contest it.
b2-10.why: The repeated subjunctive (ocurra lo que ocurra) means 'whatever happens': the outcome will not change the speaker's position.

b2-10.q: Which sentence means 'If I had known, I wouldn't have laughed'?
options: Si lo hubiera sabido, no me habría reído.
Hubiera lo sabido, no me habría reído.
Si lo habría sabido, no me hubiera reído.
Si lo supe, no me habría reído.
b2-10.why: Spanish cannot invert like 'had I known'; use si + pluperfect subjunctive + conditional perfect.

b2-10.q: Turn into a cleft that stresses who organized the shifts: «La madre de Remedios organizó los turnos.»
options: Fue la madre de Remedios quien organizó los turnos.
Fue la madre de Remedios quien organizaron los turnos.
Fue la madre de Remedios cual organizó los turnos.
Era la madre de Remedios cuando organizó los turnos.
b2-10.why: Ser (same tense as the verb: fue) + focus + quien + verb agreeing with the focus (organizó).

b2-10.q: Speaking now, make a guess: 'He must have voted for Remedios.'
b2-10.why: A guess about the recent past from now uses the future perfect: habrá votado. The others state facts or a future event.

b2-10.q: Complete: «Gane quien ___, mañana seguiremos siendo vecinos.»
b2-10.why: The structure repeats the same subjunctive form: gane quien gane ('whoever wins').
